predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 7 Fed cuts in 2026 signals a dramatically more dovish path than currently priced. Aggressive easing expectations pull front-end and long-end yields lower, lifting long-duration Treasury prices. TLT is the most liquid, direct proxy for shifting rate-cut expectations.

predictions.reasoning: An abrupt jump in expectations of 7 cuts implies a much lower future rate path, which typically weakens the dollar via narrowing rate differentials. UUP is a liquid proxy for the broad dollar. Effect is weaker and noisier than the Treasury link because dollar also carries safe-haven flows if the dovishness reflects recession/crisis fears.

evidence_used: Market question implies a very dovish, tail scenario of 7 rate cuts (175bps) in 2026
Fed rate-cut expectations directly drive Treasury yields, the dollar, and rate-sensitive assets
Long-duration Treasuries and the dollar index are the most liquid, cleanest proxies for shifts in the expected Fed path
uncertainty_notes: The 700bps tradable threshold is far larger than realistic 12h moves in these liquid proxies (~20-150bps), so this is likely NOT tradable under the stated rule
7 cuts is an extreme tail; a probability move may be noise on thin prediction-market liquidity rather than genuine information
If the dovish shift reflects recession/crisis fears, equities fall and the dollar could rally on haven flows, muddying the FX mapping
Primary topic tag 'military_conflict' appears mislabeled for a Fed-cuts market, reducing confidence in metadata

llm_justification.summary: This market prices the odds of an extremely dovish Fed (7 cuts / 175bps in 2026). A sharp rise in that probability signals expectations of far more aggressive easing than currently priced, which most cleanly implies higher long-duration Treasury prices (TLT up) and a softer dollar (UUP down). Both are plausible but modest 12h moves — well below the 700bps tradable threshold — and the dollar link is ambiguous if the dovishness reflects crisis fears that trigger safe-haven buying.
key_assumptions: A sharp, persistent rise in the implied probability of 7 cuts is the triggering anomaly
The move reflects genuine dovish repricing rather than thin-liquidity noise
Rate expectations transmit to Treasuries and FX in the standard textbook direction within the 12h window
failure_modes: Realistic 12h proxy moves (~20-150bps) fall far short of the 700bps tradable bar, so the signal is untradable under the rule
The prediction-market move may be noise or a stale/already-public repricing after FOMC or CPI, with no fresh information
If 7-cut odds rise on recession/crisis fear, safe-haven dollar demand could push UUP up, reversing the FX call
Weak or conflated causality: TLT and UUP respond to many drivers, so attributing moves to this specific market is fragile
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
